cards.name: Neon tube glow
cards.summary: Type reads as a lit neon tube: a pale hot core, a saturated coloured rim and a soft halo of the same colour bleeding onto a dark wall.
use_for: night-life, gaming and event headlines on dark backgrounds
thumbnail words that must glow off a dark frame
avoid: light or white backgrounds: the halo disappears; use an outline or a shadow instead
long body copy: the glow fills the counters of small letters
print without raising Effect > Document Raster Effects Settings to 300 ppi in Illustrator: the glows are raster effects and come out coarse

effects.name: Color Overlay
effects.note: On the type layer: a very pale tint of the neon colour as the tube's hot core.

effects.name: Inner Glow
effects.note: Saturated colour just inside the letter edges, fading to the pale core (verified frame: the glow sits inside the edges with no offset).

effects.name: Outer Glow
effects.note: Tight halo around the outside of the letters in every direction, no offset; Screen because the wall is dark.

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: Distance 0 turns the shadow into a second, wider halo (a layer has only one Outer Glow); with no offset the angle has no effect.

steps.note: One layer style: these 4 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).

On the type (live or outlined) filled with the pale core tint: edge glow, Screen, 4 pt. The glow colour gclr is a FillStyle outside the Dict string: set it to the neon colour in the dialog (app.executeMenuCommand("Live Inner Glow")) or apply a saved graphic style.
Halo around the type; Screen on a dark artboard (Normal on light ones). Colour sclr set in the dialog as above; verified frame: an even halo with no offset.
Fill the artistic text with the pale core tint (Shape.Fill.ApplyUniformFill) and give it a 1-2 pt outline in the neon colour.
s.CreateDropShadow(0, 90, 22, 0, 0, neon, 4, 0, -45, 1, 1, 0): zero offset turns the shadow into an even glow around the type; Normal merge on a dark page (Multiply would darken it).

manual_steps: Illustrator: pick the glow colours in the Inner Glow / Outer Glow dialogs (or save the finished look as a graphic style and apply that by script).

cards.name: Gold metallic type
cards.summary: Polished gold lettering: a banded light-to-dark gold gradient, hard bevelled edges lit from the upper left and a short warm shadow.
avoid: thin or small type: the bevel eats the strokes; use 60 pt and up or a heavy weight
Illustrator 3D Materials 'metallic' as a gold shortcut: its render made every fill darker with no foil or highlight
real foil printing: send a spot-colour foil plate instead of a simulated gradient

effects.name: Gradient Overlay
effects.note: On the type layer. The gradient is an object a plan cannot carry: build it in the descriptor as the card's scripting shows, stops #7A4E0E 0, #F9E79F 40, #C9971C 55, #FFF3C4 72, #8A5A12 100 (banded light and dark reads as metal).

effects.name: Bevel & Emboss
effects.note: Chisel Hard inner bevel: highlights on the up-left facing edges and dark facets down-right, as in the verified frame at local angle 120; warm highlight and brown shadow keep it gold rather than grey.

effects.name: Satin
effects.note: Soft interior bands that break the gradient up like reflections (verified frame: bands follow the letter shapes).

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: Same light angle as the bevel, so the shadow falls down-right, away from the light.

steps.note: One layer style: these 4 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).
Type > Create Outlines on a copy of the headline (keep the live type hidden for edits).

Fill the outlines with a linear gradient (doc.gradients.add(), gradientStops at 0 / 40 / 55 / 72 / 100 with the same golds as the Photoshop plan), then rotate only the fill to vertical (pageItem.rotate(90, false, false, true)); the card warns that angle set before assignment is often ignored.
Edge glow in Multiply, 6 pt at 60 %: a dark amber rim (set gclr to #5A3A06 in the dialog) rounds the letter edges like a cast.
Short warm shadow 4 pt right and down (positive horz / vert = right / down, like the 7 / 7 default).
Shape.Fill.ApplyFountainFill(...) linear at 90 degrees, then add the gold stops through Fountain.Colors (or start #7A4E0E / end #FFF3C4 at minimum).

s.CreateCustomEffect('Bevel', 0, 1, 0.03, white, 100, 135.0, 45.0, dark_brown, 50): Soft Edge, offset 0.03 in, light from the upper left (verified frame: lighter facets up-left, dark down-right). Light values are sent, not read back.
Short shadow down-right (CorelDRAW y runs up, so OffsetY is negative). If CorelDRAW will not take a second effect on the bevelled text, put the shadow on a duplicate behind it.

manual_steps: Photoshop: a Gloss Contour (Ring or Cone) in the Bevel & Emboss shading panel adds the extra metallic flicker; contour curves are objects a plan cannot carry.

cards.name: Chrome horizon type
cards.summary: Mirror-chrome lettering: a white-to-steel sky gradient that snaps to a dark horizon line mid-letter, a crisp bevel and a thin dark keyline.
use_for: retro sci-fi, automotive and music titles
product names that need a hard, shiny look
avoid: Filter > Sketch > Chrome as the main look: it turns the layer into grey liquid swirls with no lettering detail (verified frame), better as a texture overlay
light backgrounds without the keyline: the white top of the letters vanishes
small text: the horizon line collapses into a grey smear

effects.name: Gradient Overlay
effects.note: Horizon gradient built in the descriptor: #FFFFFF 0, #9AA6B4 47, #1E2530 50, #6D7A88 53, #E8EEF4 100; the hard step at 47-53 is the chrome horizon.

effects.name: Bevel & Emboss
effects.note: Hard chisel edges lit from the upper left (verified light direction at 120).

effects.name: Stroke
effects.note: Thin dark keyline outside the letters so the white top reads on any background (Outside rounds outer corners slightly).

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: Falls down-right, away from the same light.

steps.note: One layer style: these 4 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).
Create Outlines on a copy of the type.
Linear gradient fill with the horizon stops (two stops a hair apart at 47 / 53 make the hard line), rotated to vertical with pageItem.rotate(90, false, false, true).
Appearance: add a 2-3 pt dark stroke (#14181E) aligned outside. The DOM holds one stroke per path; the menu id is paired from the shortcut file, not execution-confirmed.
Thin white edge glow in Screen gives the rim highlight (gclr white, set in the dialog).
Short shadow right and down.
ApplyFountainFill linear at 90 degrees, horizon stops added through Fountain.Colors; give the text a 2 pt #14181E outline.
CreateCustomEffect('Bevel', 0, 1, 0.02, white, 100, 135.0, 45.0, black, 50): narrow soft-edge bevel lit from the upper left.

manual_steps: Photoshop: a Ring gloss contour in Bevel & Emboss (an object a plan cannot carry) sharpens the mirror effect.

cards.name: 3D extruded block type
cards.summary: Headline letters get solid depth: side walls run back from each letter in a darker shade of the face colour, like chunky 3D signage.
use_for: poster and thumbnail headlines that must pop
avoid: long text: each letter's walls overlap its neighbours; keep to a few words
Photoshop alone: it has no 3D in this version; build the type in Illustrator or CorelDRAW and place it, or use the shallow stacked-shadow stand-in below
Illustrator Revolve (Classic): its scripted apply drew nothing

steps.note: On the type (fill = face colour, stroke = a darker shade: the verified render showed stroked shapes' walls take the stroke colour). Rotation keys are radians: -0.2 / -0.45 is a gentle three-quarter view; depth in pt.
Optional: Object > Expand Appearance to hand off flat art (the 3D render becomes an image plus paths).

s.CreateExtrude(0, 0, vpx, vpy, 20, 2, base, dark, 0, 45, None, False) on the artistic text: Small Back toward a vanishing point placed outside the text, below right (document units); colour shading from a mid tone to near black, as in the verified block render.

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: Shallow stand-in for real 3D: Spread 100 with Size 0 makes a solid offset copy (card). Light at 135 sends it down-right (verified frame).

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: Second instance (dropShadowMulti) 2 px further: repeat up to 10 instances at 2 px steps for about 20 px of depth.

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: Each step a little darker so the side reads as shaded; edges stair-step on diagonals beyond 1 px steps.

steps.note: One layer style: these 3 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last); the repeated Drop Shadow instances go in its dropShadowMulti list.

manual_steps: Illustrator: fine-tune light and rotation in the 3D and Materials panel (the panel route has no modal dialog).

cards.name: Flat long-shadow type
cards.summary: A hard-edged diagonal shadow runs from every letter out to the edge of the panel and fades away, the flat-design long shadow on headline type.
use_for: flat poster and social headlines on solid colour
avoid: photos or busy backgrounds: the shadow shape fights them
thin script fonts: the sweep turns into a mess of slivers
a soft realistic shadow: use a normal drop shadow

steps.note: Create Outlines, then copy the outlines behind (Paste in Back) and fill the copy with the shadow colour.
On the shadow copy: 200 copies, each 1 pt further along the diagonal. The vertical sign is not confirmed: if the copies climb, use moveV_Pts -1.
Bake the copies into paths.

Group the copies first: on the overlap plate re-render Add gave one outline-free silhouette in the topmost object's paint (identical to the Effect menu); check it on screen, then Expand Appearance again.
Shadow at 20-30 % opacity in Multiply over the panel colour (pageItem.blendingMode = BlendModes.MULTIPLY).
Clip the shadow with a copy of the background panel so it stops at the edge.

The Block Shadow card's scripted stand-in: s.CreateExtrude(4, 0, vpx, vpy, depth, 1, dark, None, 0, 45, None, False), Back Parallel with one solid side colour, point far down-right at 45 degrees. Untested: Back Parallel was not in the render test (the verified frame is Small Back).
Break Apart (Ctrl+K) the extrusion from the text, then Weld the side faces into one shadow shape.
Weld the faces.
Fade the shadow from opaque at the letters to clear at its far end (verified linear fade); set the angle along the shadow, here -45.
On a duplicate of the type layer placed below it (Duplicate Layer, id 1135).
Loop in a script: layer.duplicate(), then translate(1, 1) on the copy, about 200 times, each copy one pixel further down-right.
Merge Layers: select the copies and merge them into one shadow layer.

effects.name: Color Overlay
effects.note: Flat shadow colour on the merged layer.

effects.name: Gradient Overlay
effects.note: Second style on the same layer: a gradient from the shadow colour to the panel colour along the shadow (stops set in the descriptor) makes it fade out.

steps.note: One layer style: these 2 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).

manual_steps: CorelDRAW by hand: the Block Shadow tool draws the same solid shadow in one drag (it has no scripting member).

cards.name: Offset outline with hard shadow
cards.summary: Retro sign-painter type: the letters carry a thin outline set slightly away from them (a gap in the background colour) and a solid, unblurred offset shadow.
avoid: tight letter spacing: the outlines merge into one blob; open the tracking first
a soft look: this is deliberately hard-edged; use a blurred drop shadow instead

effects.name: Stroke
effects.note: Stroke 1, Outside, in the background colour: this is the gap.

effects.name: Stroke
effects.note: Stroke 2 (frameFXMulti), stacked below stroke 1 and wider, so only its outer 4 px show as the offset outline.

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: Spread 100 + Size 0 = a solid offset copy of letters plus strokes, down-right (light at 135, as in the verified frame).

steps.note: One layer style: these 3 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last); the repeated Stroke instances go in its frameFXMulti list.
Appearance: add a stroke (it lands on top of the existing stroke; drag it below the fill), background colour, 8 pt aligned outside: the gap.
Add a second stroke under it, dark, 16 pt: its outer 8 pt is the outline. Saving the finished stack as a graphic style lets a script apply it in one call.
Add a fill (it lands on top of the existing fill; drag it to the bottom of the stack), dark, for the hard shadow.
On that bottom fill only: grow it to match the outline (10 pt; verified: shapes grow evenly, square corners at jntp 2).
Also on the bottom fill: move it 8 pt right and down, no extra copies, so it sits behind as a solid offset shadow (vertical sign unconfirmed: flip moveV_Pts if it moves up).
Duplicate the text twice; work back to front: dark ring copy at the back, gap copy in the middle, original on top.
On the back copy: one outside contour step in the dark outline colour, wide enough to clear the gap.
On the middle copy: one outside step in the background colour, half that offset: the gap.
On the back copy: hard shadow (Feather 0, full opacity) down-right.

manual_steps: Illustrator: building the appearance stack (extra strokes and fills, effects on one fill) is panel work; do it once by hand and save it as a graphic style for scripts.

cards.name: Letterpress deboss
cards.summary: Type looks pressed into the paper: a soft shadow inside the top edges of the letters and a faint light lip along their bottom edges.
use_for: stationery, invitations and premium packaging mock-ups
subtle titles on paper or card textures
avoid: dark text on a light page with strong settings: it turns into a grey blur; keep the type close to the paper colour
busy photographic backgrounds: the effect needs a flat or lightly textured surface

effects.name: Inner Shadow
effects.note: Light from the top: the shadow lies inside the top edges, the edges that face the light (the verified frame at 120 put it along the up-left edges).

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: A white 'shadow' 1 px below the letters (it falls away from the light) is the lit bottom lip of the impression.

effects.name: Color Overlay
effects.note: Optional: tint the type a shade darker than the paper so it reads as an ink-free impression.

steps.note: One layer style: these 3 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).
Dark edge glow in Multiply (gclr a dark paper shade, set in the dialog): darkens inside the letter edges. Illustrator has no inner shadow, so this darkens every edge evenly, not just the top.
White shadow 1 pt below in Screen (sclr white, set in the dialog) for the light lip.
s.CreateInnerShadow(60, 4, 0, -0.02, black, 4, 0, 9, -1): an offset downward darkens the top inner edges (verified frame: offset down-right darkened the top and left edges).
White lip just below: on a duplicate behind the text if CorelDRAW will not stack it with the inner shadow on one object.

cards.name: Glitch RGB split
cards.summary: Digital-error type: red and cyan copies of the letters slip sideways out of register, and horizontal bands of the word jump left or right.
use_for: tech, gaming and music headlines on dark backgrounds
title cards for explainers about software
avoid: light backgrounds: Screen fringes vanish on white (use Multiply with cyan / magenta copies there)
body text and anything that must be read quickly or by screen readers as an image
people with photosensitivity in motion versions: keep the split static or slow

steps.note: Duplicate the white type layer (on a near-black background): copy 1 is the active layer.

steps.name: Color Overlay
steps.note: Copy 1 turns pure red.

Copy 1 layer in Screen: overlaps with the white type stay white, only the slipped edge shows red. The render matched the Screen formula; the card's 'wrong' verdict refers to an outdated plate sentence.
Duplicate copy 1: copy 2 is the active layer, already in Screen; its own layer style comes next, so copy 1 stays red.

steps.name: Color Overlay
steps.note: Copy 2 turns cyan (this overlay replaces the red one copy 2 inherited).
translate(-6, 0) on the red copy and translate(6, 0) on the cyan copy.
Merge Visible into one layer (or stamp a merged copy) for the band shift.
Square wave with almost no vertical scale shifts horizontal bands sideways: the slice glitch. Untested: the verified frame used a sine wave; the square type was not rendered.
Create Outlines of the white type, then copy and Paste in Front twice.
Paste in Front: the two copies sit exactly on the original; fill one #FF0000 and one #00FFFF by script.
Both copies in Screen (pageItem.blendingMode = BlendModes.SCREEN), then translate(-4, 0) and translate(4, 0).
Duplicate the white text twice and convert both copies to lenses as below; move one 0.04 in left and one right.

s.CreateLens(4, 100, red) on the left copy: it adds red to what lies under it, so over the white letters it stays white and over the dark page the slipped edge goes red (verified frame: colour added like light, whites stay white).
Same on the right copy with cyan.
Optional: Convert to Bitmap of the group for pixel effects.
Optional: light horizontal smear (verified: streaks blown out of the edges).

cards.name: Die-cut sticker type
cards.summary: The word sits on a thick white rounded border that follows the letter shapes, lifted off the page by a soft shadow, like a vinyl sticker.
use_for: social and thumbnail call-outs on photos
labels, price flags and merch mock-ups
avoid: thin borders: under about 8 px the shape looks like a stroke, not a sticker
white pages: add a light grey or the shadow carries the whole effect
real cut files: build the cut line as a vector contour, not a pixel stroke

effects.name: Stroke
effects.note: Thick white Outside stroke; its rounded outer corners (verified) are what make it read as a die-cut.

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: The shadow follows the stroked silhouette and falls down-right, away from the light.

steps.note: One layer style: these 2 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).
Create Outlines, group, and Paste in Back a copy for the sticker base.
On the back copy filled white: grow it 12 pt (verified: shapes grow evenly; jntp 2 gave square corners, so round the joins in the dialog if wanted).
Soft shadow on the white base, right and down.
One outside contour step in white with round corners: the sticker outline (card: Steps 1 for a sticker outline; verified as a vector glow / sticker look).
Break Apart (Ctrl+K) so the white contour is its own shape.
Soft shadow on the white contour shape, down-right.

cards.name: Retro 80s sunset chrome
cards.summary: Arched headline with a sunset gradient face, a dark purple keyline, a hot-pink glow and a hard offset shadow, the synthwave title look.
avoid: corporate or serious news contexts
more than one arched line: stacked warps fight each other; arch the main word only

steps.note: On the type layer: textItem.warpStyle = WarpStyle.ARC, warpBend about 25 (the Type > Warp Text dialog, id 2218, by hand).

effects.name: Gradient Overlay
effects.note: Sunset stops set in the descriptor: #2B0B5A 0, #FF2E9A 55, #FFB000 100 (bottom to top).

effects.name: Stroke
effects.note: Dark purple keyline.

effects.name: Outer Glow
effects.note: Pink halo on the dark sky.

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: Hard cyan copy 8 px straight down (light from the top), the retro offset.

steps.note: One layer style: these 4 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).
Effect > Warp > Arc on the type: Bend 0.25, horizontal.
Sunset linear gradient fill (stops as in the Photoshop plan), rotated to vertical.
Dark purple 3 pt stroke, outside.
Pink halo (sclr set in the dialog), Screen on a dark artboard.
s.CreateEnvelope(3, 2, False): bends the text into a rounded envelope (verified on the star; for a cleaner arch use CreateEnvelopeFromShape with an arch outline).
Convert to Curves bakes the envelope so the extrusion can follow.
ApplyFountainFill linear at 90 degrees, sunset stops through Fountain.Colors; 2 pt dark purple outline.
Short Small Back extrusion straight down for the retro depth (vanishing point below the text).

manual_steps: Photoshop: Warp Text bend is easiest to judge by eye in its dialog (Type > Warp Text).
